description: The SSA is the World Health Organization's system for recording attacks on health care, meaning violence, threats or obstruction that interfere with health services, in countries facing emergencies. It is run by WHO's Health Emergencies Programme under its Attacks on Health Care initiative and was launched in December 2019. Each attack record gives its date and time, country, certainty level (from rumour to confirmed), attack type, numbers killed and injured, what was affected (facilities, ambulances and transport, personnel, supplies, warehouses, patients), the type of facility, and any abduction, arrest or detention of health workers or patients. The public dashboard covers all monitored countries; downloadable series are the Ukraine data from February 2022, with about 3,300 attacks and updated this week, and a historic file of 3,018 verified attacks from 2017 to 2021. The files are free and available to download from the Humanitarian Data Exchange under CC BY or CC BY-IGO. Caveats: attacks are counted at country level without coordinates in the files read, certainty levels must be filtered, and the full global table is shown only through the dashboard. Simulation uses: estimating the rate at which health facilities and ambulances are damaged or disrupted in conflict, setting disruption scenarios for health service continuity, and validating models of conflict impacts on care. Related records: the Gaza hospital attacks data (data-gaza-attacks-on-hospitals-2023-2025) and the explosive weapons and health facilities data (data-ewipa-explosive-weapons-health-facilities).
